facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Debt sits in separate perimeters. The senior notes are guaranteed by the operating subsidiaries but not by the financial services subsidiaries, the mortgage repurchase facilities belong to the financial services business and are not guaranteed by the company, and the company's own leverage measure excludes both construction loans and repurchase facilities, so consolidated debt and homebuilding debt differ by design. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 66.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The case that the set is stronger than it looks is that the filings describe the debt terms, the guarantor structure and the covenant types in detail and report compliance with every covenant, so the missing documents may confirm rather than change the picture. The case against is that covenant levels, step-downs and the financial covenants revised by the September 2026 amendment are not printed, so headroom cannot be measured. The executed credit agreement and amendment, the two indentures, the 2026 proxy statement, a rating report and dated quotes would move the conditional modules to ready, and a leverage or coverage test with thin headroom would make the covenant detail the first priority. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for a better credit view is asset and equity cover: inventories of USD 3,744.02 million are 2.07x total debt, equity is USD 2,561 million, the issuer net homebuilding debt to net capital is 34.9%, covenants are reported as met, no senior note matures before 2029 and the revolver was enlarged and extended. This case wins if inventories turn to cash at book value without further impairment, which needs margin to stabilise: GAAP homebuilding gross margin was 15.0% in Q3 2026 against 17.9% a year earlier, after USD 19.61 million of inventory impairment. Another quarter of negative operating cash flow with the revolver rising again would confirm the bearish view, and a recovery in deliveries and margin that lifts EBITDA while inventory shrinks would reverse it. tables.title: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Cash interest paid for the interim periods and in the cash flow statement is not printed in any filing; the annual report prints only approximately USD 78.9 million for 2024 and USD 81.3 million for 2025 in its debt note and a risk factor, so the Cash Interest Paid row is Not supplied for every interim column and interim EBITDA over cash interest is Not calculable; this corrects the Source readiness statement that no such figure exists. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain interim interest paid or use the labelled capitalised-interest proxy. - A stand-alone fourth quarter 2025 income statement, cash flow and balance sheet are not printed, so the fourth-quarter revenue and EBITDA are derived by subtraction and the cash flow columns carry year-to-date periods only. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the fourth quarter 2025 earnings release. - The maturity ladder at 2026-09-30 is not printed and the split of the drawn revolver between the 2028 and 2030 tranches is not stated, so the maturities chart is drawn at 2025-12-31 and the revolver bar of 2028 is superseded by the September 2026 amendment. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the executed amendment and a current maturity schedule. - Letters of credit of USD 42.3 million are stated under various facilities without a split, so undrawn revolver capacity is not net of any letters drawn on the revolver; the revolver has a USD 250.0 million letter of credit sublimit. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain a letters of credit schedule by facility. - Other financing obligations of USD 44.089 million combine secured borrowings and insurance premium notes with no stated rank, maturity or split, so they are left out of the debt stack and their maturity is not placed. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the note detail. - HistoryMaker acquired earnings, working capital, assumed liabilities, final purchase accounting and any holdback or adjustment are not supplied, so pro forma leverage is overstated against a denominator without the acquired EBITDA. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the purchase agreement, the closing report and the first purchase accounting. - Covenant levels, definitions and the revisions made by the September 2026 amendment are not printed, so no covenant headroom is stated. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the executed credit agreement and amendment. - The annual report FY2023 columns are not extracted because the snapshot window starts at FY2024; the 2027 and 2030 years of the maturity ladder print dashes and are stated as zero because the printed total equals the sum of the other years. Severity: Low. Action: None needed for this window. - Lines a filing prints as a dash (for example cash paid for income taxes in the first quarter of 2026 and 2025, Century Living and Corporate revenue in the segment tables, multi-family sales revenue in FY2024) are Not supplied rather than zero, and lines a filing does not print (for example the multi-family revenue lines in the quarterly income statements and the senior notes issuance lines in quarters before they occurred) are Not supplied for that filing. Severity: Low. Action: None; presentation difference between filings. - The FY2024 revolver commitment of USD 900.0 million is taken from the stated increase to USD 1.0 billion on 2025-04-22 and is not printed at 2024-12-31. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the 2024 credit agreement terms. - Quarterly adjusted EBITDA for the first three quarters of 2026 sums to USD 197.011 million against USD 197.013 million reported for nine months, a difference of USD 0.002 million from rounding in the interest and depreciation lines. Severity: Low. Action: None; use each period own reconciliation. - The annual report groups other financing obligations of USD 111.82 million at 2025-12-31 as one line while the quarterly reports split it into construction loans of USD 90.269 million and other financing obligations of USD 21.551 million. Severity: Low. Action: Use the quarterly grouping. - Guarantor names and executed terms are not supplied, so the ranking in the debt stack rests on the filing statements that the senior notes are unsecured senior obligations effectively subordinated to secured debt of the guarantors. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the guarantor list and the indentures.

citations.quote: Century Communities is a large, affordability-focused US homebuilder with no sponsor and no controlling holder named in the filings, so creditors depend on management discipline and public-company controls and not on equity support, and this module rates governance risk as medium.

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: The main creditor risks sit in the business and in capital allocation, not in ownership: prices and margins fell through 2026, West inventory was impaired, a third cash acquisition closed on 2026-10-07 and shareholder payments continued while the revolver was drawn. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business is a high-volume, affordability-weighted homebuilder, so creditor cash flow depends on selling prices, incentives and inventory turns and not on contracted revenue. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against a medium rating is that governance looks cleaner than the business. Controls are effective, the audit opinion is unqualified, no sponsor extracts fees or dividends, the 2025 refinancing replaced the 2027 notes at par with notes due 2033, and the revolver was enlarged and extended on 2026-09-30 with new lenders, which signals lender support. The case for a higher rating is the 2026 pattern of paying shareholders and buying another builder while operating cash flow was negative. The view would move to low if operating cash flow again covered shareholder payments and the HistoryMaker purchase proved leverage-neutral, and to high if repurchases continued as liquidity tightened, if the covenants revised on 2026-09-30 proved tighter than the filings imply, or if the proxy statement showed value passing to insiders. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage has moved from comfortable to high because earnings fell while debt grew. Total debt was 7.68x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, against 5.07x at FY2025 and 2.83x at FY2024, as EBITDA fell 54.77% and total debt rose USD 369.44 million in nine months. Net debt was USD 1,726.5 million, or 7.31x, and the HistoryMaker purchase of 2026-10-07 lifts it to USD 1,886.7 million and 7.99x pro forma, which overstates leverage because the acquired earnings are not yet in the denominator. On the issuer own measure, net homebuilding debt to net capital was 34.9%, against 25.9% at FY2025. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for a better view is that the balance sheet is built for this part of the cycle. Inventories cover total debt 2.07x, equity covers it 1.41x, covenants are reported as met, new lenders joined the enlarged revolver, the land pipeline was cut 24.5% in 2025 so land spend can fall, fixed cost was reduced through an 11.4% headcount cut, and the fourth quarter of 2025 turned a nine-month operating outflow into a full-year inflow. The view would improve if orders and prices stabilise so that gross margin holds at or above the 17.0% nine-month level, if fourth-quarter operating cash flow matches or beats the prior year, and if the HistoryMaker purchase proves funded from cash flow. It would worsen if the fourth quarter falls short of the guidance-implied revenue, if revolver utilisation rises above 38.00% with no seasonal reversal, if impairments spread beyond the six communities written down in the third quarter, or if repurchases continue while operating cash flow stays negative. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: A realistic downside starts with mortgage rates staying high through the winter, so orders slow and incentives rise again. The first operational break is lower average price and weaker backlog conversion, which cuts revenue and gross margin while overhead stays fixed, as it did in 2026. Operating cash flow then stays negative even after the seasonal reversal, so the revolver stays drawn and undrawn capacity of USD 744.0 million falls; if the HistoryMaker purchase was paid from the revolver, which the filings do not say, capacity would be USD 583.8 million. Management levers are slower land spend, no repurchases and lower overhead. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 months because no bond matures before 2029 and the revolver is extended to 2030, but leverage would rise and covenant headroom is not known. The observable triggers are fourth-quarter operating cash flow, revolver utilisation and gross margin. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Century Communities presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, asset cover and a long bond ladder, but credit quality is constrained by falling margins, negative cash conversion and rising leverage. Cash-flow durability appears weak at present because price declines flow through a fixed cost base into a working-capital build financed on the revolver. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the fourth-quarter cash reversal and on keeping the revolver available until the 2029 notes. The primary downside path is price and incentive pressure that holds margin low while borrowing rises. Further analysis would require covenant levels, HistoryMaker earnings and funding, and holders above 5%. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: cash conversion. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

# Century Communities, Inc. (ccs): source readiness as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Century Communities, Inc. (issuer id ccs), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the readiness of the seven supplied filings and earnings releases for financial foundation, business and governance, and fundamental credit work on the consolidated registrant. No executed debt document, rating, dated market quote, peer filing or portfolio input was supplied.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases support the requested financial, business and credit work on Century Communities, Inc. through the quarter ended 2026-09-30, but not covenant or ratings conclusions, so every later view rests on the issuer's own disclosure alone.

The reporting entity is the consolidated registrant itself, so there is no parent or group perimeter to separate. The binding constraints are that no executed debt document, rating, dated market quote or proxy statement was supplied, and that the HistoryMaker acquisition of October 2026 sits outside every reported balance.
### Key findings

The documents cover fiscal 2025, the first three quarters of 2026 and the nine months to 2026-09-30, each with year-ago comparatives, so quarter and year-to-date figures can be kept apart. The fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed on its own; it can be obtained only by subtracting nine-month 2025 from full-year 2025, and the readiness tests show that route works for net income and that the three 2026 quarters add up to the nine-month total.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-3.

Debt can be listed instrument by instrument from the notes: two fixed-rate senior note series, a senior unsecured revolving credit facility, secured construction loans, mortgage repurchase facilities and other financing obligations, and the listed instruments add up to the balance sheet debt lines at both 2026-09-30 and 2025-12-31. The contract terms behind them, meaning covenant levels, redemption schedules and guarantor identities, are not in the set because no executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 14–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 74; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-6.

Debt sits in separate perimeters. The senior notes are guaranteed by the operating subsidiaries but not by the financial services subsidiaries, the mortgage repurchase facilities belong to the financial services business and are not guaranteed by the company, and the company's own leverage measure excludes both construction loans and repurchase facilities, so consolidated debt and homebuilding debt differ by design.

The newest events are dated and must stay apart from period figures. The revolving credit facility was enlarged and extended on 2026-09-30, the last day of the quarter, and the HistoryMaker asset acquisition closed on 2026-10-07, after the balance sheet date, with purchase accounting unfinished and no pro forma balance sheet in the set.

Comparability rests on definitions that changed during 2025. Adjusted EBITDA gained two add-backs, lot option abandonments from the third quarter and stock-based compensation from the fourth quarter, and inventory impairment moved into cost of home sales, each with earlier periods recast; each supplied document states its comparatives on the recast basis, so a series drawn only from them is internally consistent.

Governance evidence is thin. Directors, executive officers, compensation and ownership are incorporated by reference to a 2026 proxy statement that was not supplied, which leaves the officers named on the signature pages and releases and a risk factor stating that the Executive Chairman and the Chief Executive Officer, who are brothers, together held 13.9% of the common stock on 2025-12-31.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The case that the set is stronger than it looks is that the filings describe the debt terms, the guarantor structure and the covenant types in detail and report compliance with every covenant, so the missing documents may confirm rather than change the picture. The case against is that covenant levels, step-downs and the financial covenants revised by the September 2026 amendment are not printed, so headroom cannot be measured. The executed credit agreement and amendment, the two indentures, the 2026 proxy statement, a rating report and dated quotes would move the conditional modules to ready, and a leverage or coverage test with thin headroom would make the covenant detail the first priority.
### Limitations

- No executed debt document, rating, dated market quote, peer filing, proxy statement or portfolio input was supplied, so every conclusion that depends on them is conditional or stated as not established.
- The documents end with filings signed on 2026-10-28, and nothing between that date and the cutoff of 2026-11-05 was supplied, so later events are not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 74.

- The supplied pages were read as extracted visible text in which table cells fall on separate lines; row and column alignment was checked against headings and totals but not against the original layout.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage has risen sharply since FY2024 as earnings fell and borrowing grew: total debt is 7.68x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, against 5.07x at FY2025 and 2.83x at FY2024, which leaves creditors reliant on liquidity and equity rather than earnings cover.

Interest cover on reported EBITDA fell from 6.61x in FY2024 to 3.50x in FY2025 and cannot be measured on a cash basis for 2026, while nine-month operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 267.48 million funded by the revolver. The cushions are USD 744 million of undrawn revolver capacity and no senior note maturity before 2029; the HistoryMaker acquisition of 2026-10-07 adds about USD 160.2 million of net debt that the ratios do not yet reflect.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation LTM-E-9M; calculation ND-9M2026; calculation NAR-REV
### Key findings

Leverage is driven by falling earnings and a working-capital build. Total debt rose by USD 369.44 million from USD 1,443.15 million at FY2025 to USD 1,812.59 million at 2026-09-30, while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 236.05 million is 54.77% below the USD 521.9 million of FY2024. Net debt is 7.31x that EBITDA, and total debt is 6.16x issuer-adjusted EBITDA, so the conclusion survives the issuer add-backs.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 65; calculation NAR-DEBT; calculation NAR-EBITDA; calculation LTM-E-9M; calculation LTM-A-9M; calculation ND-9M2026

Cash flow quality deteriorated sharply. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 267.48 million in nine months 2026 against an inflow of USD 153.08 million in FY2025, because inventories absorbed USD 403.41 million after releasing USD 41.13 million in FY2025. The revolver rose by a net USD 404.5 million while USD 27.52 million of dividends and USD 71.2 million of share repurchases were paid, which turns working capital into debt.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 108–109; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation NAR-REV; calculation FCF-9M

Cover on cash interest paid was 6.61x in FY2024 and 3.50x in FY2025, on the approximate annual figures of USD 78.9 million and USD 81.3 million that the annual report debt note prints. No interim filing prints interest paid, so interim cover rests on a labelled proxy using interest capitalised on the notes and revolver, which fell from 7.25x in FY2024 to 3.07x for the twelve months to 2026-09-30; the proxy overstates cover because it omits interest on construction loans, repurchase facilities and other debt.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation INT-9M; calculation LTM-E-9M

Liquidity is adequate but lower than at the year end. Undrawn revolver capacity was USD 744 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 948.5 million at FY2025 even after the commitment was raised from USD 1,000 million to USD 1,200 million, and cash and cash equivalents were USD 86.09 million. The repurchase facilities of USD 191.27 million and construction loans of USD 129.45 million serve the financial services and multi-family businesses and are not counted as corporate liquidity.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; calculation UD-9M2026; calculation UD-FY2025

Near-term maturities are mostly secured facilities that roll. The annual report ladder at 2025-12-31 shows USD 385.76 million due in 2026, nothing in 2027, USD 51.5 million in 2028, USD 515.33 million in 2029 and USD 500 million after 2030; the 2029 senior notes of USD 500 million are the first long-dated bullet and the 2033 senior notes the last. The September 2026 amendment moved most revolver commitments to 2030-11-01, so the 2028 bar is superseded, and no ladder at 2026-09-30 is printed.

The leverage perimeter and the EBITDA definition both matter. Consolidated total debt includes USD 191.27 million of repurchase facilities, matched by USD 186.51 million of mortgage loans held for sale, and USD 129.45 million of construction loans, while the issuer homebuilding debt of USD 1,491.87 million excludes both; its net homebuilding debt to net capital rose from 30.5% at Q1 2026 to 34.9% at Q3 2026. Reported EBITDA also adds back USD 64.13 million of interest charged through cost of sales over the last twelve months, 27.17% of the total, so a reader who treats that interest as an operating cost would see lower EBITDA and weaker cover.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation HB-9M2026; calculation CFL-1; calculation NAR-NHD

Three data points need care. The fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed and is derived by subtraction, giving revenue of USD 1,233.58 million. The EBITDA definitions changed twice in 2025 and every supplied period is stated on the recast basis. Source readiness stated that no cash paid for interest figure exists in the sources; that is wrong for fiscal years, because the annual report prints approximately USD 78.9 million for 2024 and USD 81.3 million for 2025 in its debt note, though not in the cash flow statement and not for interim periods.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 91–92; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation Q4-R; Source readiness (CP-0)

The revolving credit facility was amended on 2026-09-30, raising commitments from USD 1,000 million to USD 1,200 million and extending most of them to 2030-11-01, which the liquidity at 2026-09-30 reflects. The HistoryMaker acquisition closed on 2026-10-07 for initial cash consideration of about USD 160.2 million and is excluded from every period figure; adding it to net debt gives USD 1,886.7 million and 7.99x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, which overstates leverage because the acquired earnings are not in the denominator.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation PF-ND; calculation PF-LEV
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a better credit view is asset and equity cover: inventories of USD 3,744.02 million are 2.07x total debt, equity is USD 2,561 million, the issuer net homebuilding debt to net capital is 34.9%, covenants are reported as met, no senior note matures before 2029 and the revolver was enlarged and extended. This case wins if inventories turn to cash at book value without further impairment, which needs margin to stabilise: GAAP homebuilding gross margin was 15.0% in Q3 2026 against 17.9% a year earlier, after USD 19.61 million of inventory impairment. Another quarter of negative operating cash flow with the revolver rising again would confirm the bearish view, and a recovery in deliveries and margin that lifts EBITDA while inventory shrinks would reverse it.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation NAR-INV
### Limitations

- Cash interest paid is available only as approximate annual figures printed outside the cash flow statement, so interim cover is a proxy and the fiscal-year cover ratios carry the rounding of those figures.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 130

- No stand-alone fourth quarter of 2025, no maturity ladder at 2026-09-30 and no pro forma balance sheet for the HistoryMaker acquisition are printed, so the quarterly series, the maturity chart and the post-balance-sheet view rest on subtraction, on the annual ladder or on stated consideration.

- Statements are in USD thousands as printed and the money tables in USD millions; a line a filing prints as a dash is treated as not supplied rather than as zero, and a line a filing does not print is not supplied for that filing.

## Gaps

- Cash interest paid for the interim periods and in the cash flow statement is not printed in any filing; the annual report prints only approximately USD 78.9 million for 2024 and USD 81.3 million for 2025 in its debt note and a risk factor, so the Cash Interest Paid row is Not supplied for every interim column and interim EBITDA over cash interest is Not calculable; this corrects the Source readiness statement that no such figure exists. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain interim interest paid or use the labelled capitalised-interest proxy.

- A stand-alone fourth quarter 2025 income statement, cash flow and balance sheet are not printed, so the fourth-quarter revenue and EBITDA are derived by subtraction and the cash flow columns carry year-to-date periods only. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the fourth quarter 2025 earnings release.

- The maturity ladder at 2026-09-30 is not printed and the split of the drawn revolver between the 2028 and 2030 tranches is not stated, so the maturities chart is drawn at 2025-12-31 and the revolver bar of 2028 is superseded by the September 2026 amendment. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the executed amendment and a current maturity schedule.

- Letters of credit of USD 42.3 million are stated under various facilities without a split, so undrawn revolver capacity is not net of any letters drawn on the revolver; the revolver has a USD 250.0 million letter of credit sublimit. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain a letters of credit schedule by facility.

- Other financing obligations of USD 44.089 million combine secured borrowings and insurance premium notes with no stated rank, maturity or split, so they are left out of the debt stack and their maturity is not placed. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the note detail.

- HistoryMaker acquired earnings, working capital, assumed liabilities, final purchase accounting and any holdback or adjustment are not supplied, so pro forma leverage is overstated against a denominator without the acquired EBITDA. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the purchase agreement, the closing report and the first purchase accounting.

- Covenant levels, definitions and the revisions made by the September 2026 amendment are not printed, so no covenant headroom is stated. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the executed credit agreement and amendment.

- The annual report FY2023 columns are not extracted because the snapshot window starts at FY2024; the 2027 and 2030 years of the maturity ladder print dashes and are stated as zero because the printed total equals the sum of the other years. Severity: Low. Action: None needed for this window.

- Lines a filing prints as a dash (for example cash paid for income taxes in the first quarter of 2026 and 2025, Century Living and Corporate revenue in the segment tables, multi-family sales revenue in FY2024) are Not supplied rather than zero, and lines a filing does not print (for example the multi-family revenue lines in the quarterly income statements and the senior notes issuance lines in quarters before they occurred) are Not supplied for that filing. Severity: Low. Action: None; presentation difference between filings.

- The FY2024 revolver commitment of USD 900.0 million is taken from the stated increase to USD 1.0 billion on 2025-04-22 and is not printed at 2024-12-31. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the 2024 credit agreement terms.

- Quarterly adjusted EBITDA for the first three quarters of 2026 sums to USD 197.011 million against USD 197.013 million reported for nine months, a difference of USD 0.002 million from rounding in the interest and depreciation lines. Severity: Low. Action: None; use each period own reconciliation.

- The annual report groups other financing obligations of USD 111.82 million at 2025-12-31 as one line while the quarterly reports split it into construction loans of USD 90.269 million and other financing obligations of USD 21.551 million. Severity: Low. Action: Use the quarterly grouping.

- Guarantor names and executed terms are not supplied, so the ranking in the debt stack rests on the filing statements that the senior notes are unsecured senior obligations effectively subordinated to secured debt of the guarantors. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the guarantor list and the indentures.

# Century Communities, Inc. (ccs): business and governance as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Century Communities, Inc. (issuer id ccs), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business, ownership, operating model and governance of the consolidated registrant and the transactions that changed its capital structure, read from the seven supplied filings and earnings releases to the quarter ended 2026-09-30.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Century Communities is a large, affordability-focused US homebuilder with no sponsor and no controlling holder named in the filings, so creditors depend on management discipline and public-company controls and not on equity support, and this module rates governance risk as medium.

The main creditor risks sit in the business and in capital allocation, not in ownership: prices and margins fell through 2026, West inventory was impaired, a third cash acquisition closed on 2026-10-07 and shareholder payments continued while the revolver was drawn.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation CALC-8; calculation CALC-9
### Key findings

The business is a high-volume, affordability-weighted homebuilder, so creditor cash flow depends on selling prices, incentives and inventory turns and not on contracted revenue. The company builds in 16 states under two brands, about 94% of 2025 deliveries were priced below the Federal Housing Administration loan limits, and about 99% were move-in ready homes that shorten the cash cycle but leave buyers dependent on mortgage affordability.

Regional concentration is moderate, but the West is the weak spot. No homebuilding segment exceeded 23.13% of 2025 revenue, and financial services and multi-family rentals together contributed only 4.45%. In the first nine months of 2026 West revenue fell 17.91%, its pre-tax income fell to USD 6.62 million from USD 67.59 million, and it carried USD 19.1 million of the USD 19.6 million of inventory impairment recorded in the third quarter.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 120–121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-11

Price has fallen faster than volume, which is why margins are under pressure. The average price of new homes delivered fell 10.2% in the third quarter of 2026 to USD 345.0 thousand while deliveries slipped only 1.77%, homebuilding gross margin fell to 15.0% from 17.9%, and the company says it raised incentives to lift sales pace. Orders equalled 1.05x deliveries over nine months and backlog value is flat at USD 413.96 million against USD 416.92 million a year earlier, so the volume base is holding but at lower prices.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-5

The land position gives flexibility but is long relative to sales pace. Lots owned and controlled covered about 6.10 years of trailing deliveries at 2026-09-30, against 5.86 years at 2025-12-31, after the position shrank 24.5% during 2025 and with 45.1% held under options. Options limit capital at risk, but terminated contracts cost USD 11.2 million in 2025 and Texas holds the largest share of lots.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-12

Growth has become acquisition-led, which adds integration and funding risk to a cyclical business. Three cash acquisitions closed since January 2024 for roughly USD 320.6 million, the latest being HistoryMaker Homes on 2026-10-07 for initial cash of USD 160.2 million. It adds 29 communities, about 8.45% of the company selling communities, and management says it triples Dallas deliveries, but purchase accounting is unfinished and the filings state neither how it was funded nor what it earns.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ccs-20261028xex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation CALC-7

Ownership is public with founder-managers holding a minority stake, which keeps incentives with shareholders but gives creditors no sponsor or parent behind the notes. The Executive Chairman and the Chief Executive Officer are brothers and founders, sit on the board and together held 13.9% of the stock at 2025-12-31, and the company itself says they have significant influence. Other large holders, board composition and related-party dealings are not established because Part III is incorporated by reference to a proxy statement.

Capital allocation is the clearest area to monitor, because shareholder payments have continued while operating cash flow is negative. In 2025 repurchases and dividends of USD 178.37 million exceeded full-year operating cash flow of USD 153.08 million. In the first nine months of 2026 they were USD 98.72 million against an operating outflow of USD 267.48 million, with the revolver up by a net USD 404.5 million; part of the outflow is seasonal, since the same period of 2025 also showed one of USD 57.65 million, but the 2026 gap is far larger. The dividend was raised 10% to USD 0.32 a quarter and 28.77% of the repurchase authorisation is unused.

The control environment is a relative strength. The auditor has served since 2013, gave an unqualified opinion and found internal control over financial reporting effective, and legal proceedings are described as ordinary course. The one critical audit matter is the judgement on inventory impairment indicators, which is exactly where the 2026 charge arose, so reported earnings carry estimate risk even with sound controls.

Debt sits partly outside the note guarantee group, so structure matters as much as size. Substantially all wholly-owned operating subsidiaries guarantee the notes, the financial services subsidiaries do not, and the mortgage repurchase facilities are not guaranteed by the parent, while the parent guarantees portions of the Century Living construction loans, which stood at USD 129.45 million at 2026-09-30.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a medium rating is that governance looks cleaner than the business. Controls are effective, the audit opinion is unqualified, no sponsor extracts fees or dividends, the 2025 refinancing replaced the 2027 notes at par with notes due 2033, and the revolver was enlarged and extended on 2026-09-30 with new lenders, which signals lender support. The case for a higher rating is the 2026 pattern of paying shareholders and buying another builder while operating cash flow was negative. The view would move to low if operating cash flow again covered shareholder payments and the HistoryMaker purchase proved leverage-neutral, and to high if repurchases continued as liquidity tightened, if the covenants revised on 2026-09-30 proved tighter than the filings imply, or if the proxy statement showed value passing to insiders.

### Limitations

- The ownership conclusion rests on one risk-factor sentence dated 2025-12-31, so the view that no single holder controls the company would change if a holder above 5% exists or the stake of the founders has moved since then.

- The description of the business, its affordability focus and the benefits of HistoryMaker are management statements that the filings do not test against outside data, so the conclusion that the model suits a downturn is a reading of company claims.
- The 2026 operating figures cover three seasonal quarters, so the conclusions on price, margin and West weakness describe direction and could reverse in a stronger fourth quarter.

- The HistoryMaker purchase is described only by cash price, community count and a delivery comment, so the conclusion that it raises integration and funding risk cannot be sized without its earnings, funding and debt effect.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The latest transaction is the HistoryMaker Homes asset acquisition, completed on 2026-10-07 after the balance sheet date for initial cash consideration of about USD 160.2 million, subject to customary holdbacks and post-closing adjustments. It adds 29 active communities in the greater Dallas area to the Texas segment, and the company states that the purchase accounting is not final. The filings do not state how the cash was funded or what the business earns.

The revolving credit facility was amended on 2026-09-30, raising commitments from USD 1.0 billion to USD 1.2 billion. Participating lenders extended maturity, so USD 1.1 billion now matures on 2030-11-01 and USD 100.0 million stays at 2028-11-01. The amendment also added lenders, revised certain financial covenants whose levels are not printed, and removed a 0.10% spread adjustment on SOFR-based borrowings. Drawings were USD 456.0 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 51.5 million at 2025-12-31.

The only new bond issue in the period is the 2033 senior notes of USD 500.0 million, sold at par in September 2025 with net proceeds of USD 493.1 million. In the same month the company extinguished USD 500.0 million of 2027 senior notes at par, a payment of USD 511.4 million including accrued interest, so the refinancing extended maturity without adding principal. The new notes are unsecured, are guaranteed by the operating subsidiaries and give holders a put on a change of control.

Earlier transactions shaped the current group. The company bought Landmark Homes of Tennessee on 2024-01-22 for about USD 33.4 million and Anglia Homes on 2024-07-31 for about USD 127.0 million, both in cash, raised the revolver from USD 900.0 million to USD 1.0 billion on 2025-04-22, and sold a mortgage servicing portfolio for USD 46.9 million in cash in 2025. No sponsor transaction, leveraged buyout or debt-funded dividend appears in the filings.

# Century Communities, Inc. (ccs): fundamental credit as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Century Communities, Inc. (issuer id ccs), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the fundamental credit profile of the consolidated registrant, synthesised from the seven supplied filings and earnings releases and the three earlier module outputs, to the quarter ended 2026-09-30 and the acquisition of 2026-10-07.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Fundamental credit quality is adequate but weakening: inventory, equity and a long bond ladder support creditors, while earnings, margins and cash conversion have deteriorated enough that leverage has more than doubled in two years and now leans on a revolver that is increasingly drawn.

The primary downside path is further price and incentive cuts that compress margin while inventory and acquisitions keep absorbing revolver capacity; company guidance already implies a fourth quarter well below last year, so this module treats cash conversion, and not asset cover, as the measure that decides the view.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ccs-20261028xex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ccs-20261028xex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-6
### Key findings

Leverage has moved from comfortable to high because earnings fell while debt grew. Total debt was 7.68x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, against 5.07x at FY2025 and 2.83x at FY2024, as EBITDA fell 54.77% and total debt rose USD 369.44 million in nine months. Net debt was USD 1,726.5 million, or 7.31x, and the HistoryMaker purchase of 2026-10-07 lifts it to USD 1,886.7 million and 7.99x pro forma, which overstates leverage because the acquired earnings are not yet in the denominator. On the issuer own measure, net homebuilding debt to net capital was 34.9%, against 25.9% at FY2025.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation CF-1; calculation CF-2; calculation CF-3; calculation CF-4; calculation CF-5; calculation CF-6

Earnings power has fallen faster than revenue, which shows high operating leverage. Last-twelve-months revenue is 13.26% below FY2024 but issuer-adjusted EBITDA is 49.59% lower, about 3.74x the revenue decline, because selling, general and administrative cost fell only 1.94% in nine months while home sales revenue fell 12.12%. Homebuilding gross margin was 15.0% in the third quarter against 17.9%, after USD 19.6 million of impairment, and the company attributes the sales pace to higher incentives.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2

Cash conversion has turned negative and liquidity is adequate but shrinking. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 267.48 million in nine months against an outflow of USD 57.65 million a year earlier, as inventories absorbed USD 403.41 million, and the revolver rose by a net USD 404.5 million. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a better view is that the balance sheet is built for this part of the cycle. Inventories cover total debt 2.07x, equity covers it 1.41x, covenants are reported as met, new lenders joined the enlarged revolver, the land pipeline was cut 24.5% in 2025 so land spend can fall, fixed cost was reduced through an 11.4% headcount cut, and the fourth quarter of 2025 turned a nine-month operating outflow into a full-year inflow. The view would improve if orders and prices stabilise so that gross margin holds at or above the 17.0% nine-month level, if fourth-quarter operating cash flow matches or beats the prior year, and if the HistoryMaker purchase proves funded from cash flow. It would worsen if the fourth quarter falls short of the guidance-implied revenue, if revolver utilisation rises above 38.00% with no seasonal reversal, if impairments spread beyond the six communities written down in the third quarter, or if repurchases continue while operating cash flow stays negative.

### Limitations

- The conclusion that cash conversion can recover in the fourth quarter rests on one year of seasonal comparison and on company guidance, so it would change if receipts or deliveries follow a different pattern.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ccs-20261028xex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4

- Asset cover is measured at book value because the filings give no appraisal of land or homes, so the conclusion that inventory protects creditors could be overstated if write-downs spread beyond the six communities already impaired.

- Liquidity headroom is measured against committed revolver capacity and not against covenant limits, so the conclusion that liquidity is adequate cannot say how far earnings could fall before a covenant restricts borrowing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17
- The sector and competitive conclusions rest on the company own risk disclosures and statements, so they are qualitative and cannot be ranked against peers or market data.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Asset and equity cover is the first strength. Inventories of USD 3,744.02 million are 2.07x total debt and equity of USD 2,561.0 million is 1.41x debt, so creditors sit behind a large book of land and homes under construction that can be sold down if demand weakens, which supports recovery value even while earnings fall.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation CF-9

The debt ladder is the second strength. No bond matures before 2029, USD 1.1 billion of revolver commitments run to 2030-11-01 and the notes are unsecured obligations guaranteed by the operating subsidiaries, so refinancing pressure on the bonds is distant and the maturity wall is not the near-term risk.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation CALC-7

Liquidity is the third strength. Undrawn revolver capacity of USD 744.0 million and new lenders in the September 2026 amendment give room to fund the seasonal build and the HistoryMaker purchase, which keeps near-term liquidity distress unlikely if cash returns in the fourth quarter.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation CF-8

Scale and diversification are the fourth strength. No homebuilding segment exceeds 23.13% of revenue, the group builds in 16 states and about 94% of homes are priced below Federal Housing Administration limits, which spreads regional risk and targets the deepest buyer pool, though it does not protect against national rate moves.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 120–121

A flexible land model is the fifth strength. Options cover 45.1% of lots and the pipeline was cut 24.5% in 2025, so land spend can be slowed quickly and capital expenditure outside inventory is small, which helps cash generation if demand stays soft.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 47

Leverage and earnings are the first weakness. Total debt is 7.68x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA against 2.83x at FY2024 and EBITDA is 54.77% lower, so a small further earnings decline moves leverage sharply and leaves less cover for interest.

Cash conversion is the second weakness. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 267.48 million in nine months and the revolver rose by a net USD 404.5 million, so working capital is being financed with debt and the recovery depends on a fourth-quarter inflow that guidance suggests will be smaller.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation CF-7; calculation CALC-4

Acquisition-led growth is the fourth weakness. Three cash purchases since January 2024 culminated in the HistoryMaker deal for initial cash of USD 160.2 million with funding, earnings and accounting not stated, which adds integration and borrowing risk at the point of weakest earnings.

### Company description and credit linkage

Century Communities builds and sells homes, and home sales are 95.35% of revenue, with mortgage services and Colorado multi-family rentals as small additions. Revenue is transactional, not contracted: backlog covers only 1.30 months of last-twelve-months revenue, so cash flow depends on orders converting at current prices, and the affordable entry-level focus gives volume but limited pricing power. Cash-flow visibility is therefore low, debt service depends on liquidity and asset sales rather than on contracted receipts, and refinancing confidence rests on inventory cover.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation CALC-10
### Ownership and group structure

The company is public with founder-managers holding 13.9%, no sponsor and no parent. The notes are guaranteed by substantially all wholly-owned operating subsidiaries, while the financial services subsidiaries and their mortgage repurchase facilities sit outside the guarantee group and the parent guarantees portions of the multi-family construction loans. Creditors therefore rank behind secured construction and warehouse lenders on their assets, and governance risk is medium because payments to shareholders and acquisitions are discretionary and board independence is not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 82
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is cyclical, discretionary and sensitive to mortgage rates. Nine-month deliveries fell 5.38% and average price fell 7.13%, and in the third quarter price fell 10.20% against deliveries down only 1.77%, so price is now the main driver. Orders equalled 1.05x deliveries over nine months and backlog value is flat at USD 413.96 million, which supports near-term volume but not price, and cancellation risk rises with rates because contracts carry financing contingencies. Weak pricing power means revenue declines flow through to margin and cash.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation CALC-11
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are hard to defend under falling prices. Selling, general and administrative cost was 14.64% of home sales revenue in nine months against 13.12% a year earlier because it fell only 1.94%, direct construction costs have fallen but incentives and impairments offset them, and interest charged through cost of sales is added back in EBITDA. Fixed overhead and incentives make operating leverage the transmission path from price declines to lower EBITDA, which weakens interest cover and leverage together.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ccs-20261028xex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation CALC-2
### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Capital expenditure is small, so free cash flow is decided by working capital. Purchases of property and equipment were USD 21.65 million in nine months, while inventories absorbed USD 403.41 million against USD 170.15 million a year earlier, leaving operating cash flow less capital expenditure at an outflow of USD 289.12 million. Receipts concentrate in the second half, so conversion should improve seasonally, but guidance implies a smaller inflow than last year and dividends and repurchases add to cash use.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation CF-7; calculation CF-12; calculation CALC-4
### Industry forces

Rivalry is intense and barriers are low: homebuilders compete for buyers, land, labour and financing, and recent industry consolidation changes the competitive balance. Buyers hold power through mortgage affordability and incentives, substitutes include existing homes, foreclosures and rentals, and suppliers and subcontractors are not tied by long contracts, with tariffs on cabinets and lumber a cost risk. Each force acts through price and incentive levels, which feed margin, impairment and cash flow, so none is a direct default driver but all raise the sensitivity of earnings to the housing cycle.
### Macro and policy factors

Macro and policy factors are material. Mortgage rates rose further during 2026 and the company cut guidance because of them, fuel and transport costs rose with events in the Middle East, tariffs on imported cabinets and wood products took effect in late 2025, and a federal housing package became law in July 2026 with an effect the company says is uncertain. Rates feed demand and cancellations, tariffs feed cost, and both pressure margin and orders without a clear date for relief.
### Credit-translated strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats

Strengths are asset cover, the maturity ladder, liquidity, scale and a flexible land model. Weaknesses are leverage, cash conversion, margin and the cost base. Opportunities are a rate decline that revives orders and the added Dallas scale if integration is cheap, both of which would improve cash generation and leverage. Threats are further rate rises, tariff costs, more impairments and a debt-funded acquisition pattern, each of which would reduce liquidity or raise leverage.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 34
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale is strong and competitive advantage is average, with a low-cost entry-level offer but no pricing moat. Diversification is average across five regions but one product type. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because land and capital expenditure can flex while overhead did not. Margin stability and free cash flow stability are weak after the 2026 declines. The ability to refinance is average given the distant maturities, liquidity is average and shrinking, and financial policy and governance are average with a medium risk level. The trend is down on every earnings and cash measure, the supports are asset cover and maturities, and the missing datapoints are covenant levels, acquired earnings and holders above 5%.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation CF-5; calculation CF-7; calculation CF-9
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook is weaker: the company cut its 2026 delivery guidance twice and expects fourth-quarter revenue well below last year, while mortgage rates rose further. Company-specific tailwinds are a larger Dallas business, a reduced lot pipeline and an extended revolver, and headwinds are price incentives, impairments and a higher revolver balance. Over three to five years management points to undersupplied housing and favourable demographics, which would support volume, but that is a management view and it does not remove the near-term cash test.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-22_ccs-20260422xex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ccs-20261028xex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation CALC-3
### Downside scenario

A realistic downside starts with mortgage rates staying high through the winter, so orders slow and incentives rise again. The first operational break is lower average price and weaker backlog conversion, which cuts revenue and gross margin while overhead stays fixed, as it did in 2026. Operating cash flow then stays negative even after the seasonal reversal, so the revolver stays drawn and undrawn capacity of USD 744.0 million falls; if the HistoryMaker purchase was paid from the revolver, which the filings do not say, capacity would be USD 583.8 million. Management levers are slower land spend, no repurchases and lower overhead. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 months because no bond matures before 2029 and the revolver is extended to 2030, but leverage would rise and covenant headroom is not known. The observable triggers are fourth-quarter operating cash flow, revolver utilisation and gross margin.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ccs-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-12
### Overall credit view

Overall, Century Communities presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, asset cover and a long bond ladder, but credit quality is constrained by falling margins, negative cash conversion and rising leverage. Cash-flow durability appears weak at present because price declines flow through a fixed cost base into a working-capital build financed on the revolver. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the fourth-quarter cash reversal and on keeping the revolver available until the 2029 notes. The primary downside path is price and incentive pressure that holds margin low while borrowing rises. Further analysis would require covenant levels, HistoryMaker earnings and funding, and holders above 5%. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: cash conversion.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
